name: Query Optimization Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday query optimization work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical query optimization tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday query optimization work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical query optimization tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Validate query optimization outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
2. Document any non-obvious query optimization decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
3. When query optimization decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
4. When query optimization guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
5. State assumptions about query optimization explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to query optimization (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Keep query optimization changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting query optimization assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid introducing new query optimization abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of query optimization correctness.
- Do not silently drop query optimization edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for query optimization, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
